messages:
alex_k: quick heads-up — while running the long-context stress harness on Llama-2-70B-mqa we see sustained memory growth even after request completion. looks like KV pages aren't being reclaimed properly.
priya: ugh. is this the same fragmentation pattern we saw with rope-scaling? any repro steps? :eyes:
samuel: repro is straightforward — send 200 concurrent sessions with varied context lengths (4k/16k/32k) and random prompt windowing. after ~3k tokens the process RSS climbs and doesn't drop on GC. attaching small log snippet: 
```
[2025-10-12T14:23:11Z] session=203 alloc_kv=1.9G pages=47 fragments=1024
[2025-10-12T14:26:02Z] session=203 alloc_kv=2.2G pages=52 fragments=1035
[2025-10-12T14:30:00Z] session=203 freed_kv=0 pages_freed=2
[2025-10-12T14:35:00Z] session=203 alloc_kv=2.2G pages=52 fragments=1035
```
samuel: note: this only spikes on the MQA variant; vanilla GQA Llama and Mistral-8x show stable reuse.
priya: interesting — could be alignment/stride differences due to interleaving MQA heads. we did see different kv-entry sizes for MQA in profiler. do we still pick the same kernel/allocator?
perf-bot: perf summary for run 2025-10-12T14: — avg latency +3ms, token throughput -6%, peak RSS +18%, KV page reuse ratio 0.42 (expected >0.9)
devon: @alex_k can you dump per-layer kv sizes? wondering if rope scaling (positional multipliers) is causing some per-layer padding blowup.
alex_k: grabbed a per-layer snapshot. top layers have ~3x more entries due to our rope replication step when we build extended contexts. snippet: 
```
layer 34: kv_entries=1_024_000 entry_size=64 padding=16
layer 35: kv_entries=3_072_000 entry_size=64 padding=48
```
priya: that matches a bug i'd suspected — when we expand rope for MQA we replicate keys per head group but forget to compact after token eviction. effectively we create ghost entries that never map to live sessions.
samuel: repro patch idea: add a background compaction pass that walks page tables and coalesces contiguous free ranges after N frees. naive implementation reduced RSS in my local test by ~700MB.
devon: sounds promising but watch latency spikes for compaction. maybe only run during low-qps or as an async low-priority task. also we should check batching heuristics: if many small contexts batch together we trigger more frequent rope expansions.
priya: agree. short-term: 1) add compaction pass gated by qps threshold 2) add metrics for ghost-entry ratio + page-fragmentation histogram 3) canary build to dedicated pool.
alex_k: i'll open a PR with the compaction + metrics. title: "kv: mqa rope compaction + fragmentation metrics". will include unit test and a toggled feature flag.
perf-bot: deploy preview ready: job/kv-compaction/175900-pp run-id=872. initial run on staging reduced peak RSS by 14% but had two compaction pauses ~20-40ms.
samuel: those pauses are acceptable if we gate them. devon: let's also add a reuse heuristic: when a page is reclaimed, prefer reusing same physical chunk for same model variant to reduce cross-variant fragmentation. could be as simple as variant-tagged freelists.
priya: yep. variant-tagged freelist + small-size-bucket allocator. should mitigate MQA-specific padding.
alex_k: plan for rollout: canary to 10% dedicated capacity tomorrow, collect KV reuse ratio, fragmentation histogram, and latency p95 before/after. if compaction pauses >50ms or p95 regresses >5%, rollback.
devon: add a tracing hook so we can correlate compaction pauses with client-side timeouts.
priya: i'll add dashboards and alerts for ghost-entry ratio >0.2 and compaction_pause_ms >40ms.
alex_k: thanks team — i'll post PR link and prod canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:
